introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
enonce_intro_markdown: An ex-student of a school has 19200 FCFA only to buy $x$ Mathematics and $y$ English text books for the school library.
incertitudes: Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, sans total par question. Le champ points de l'exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions.

5(d) : le sujet ne dit pas si au moins un livre d'anglais doit etre achete ; reponse retenue 8 (8 livres de mathematiques, 0 d'anglais, sommet (8,0)), avec la variante 7 si y >= 1 donnee dans le corrige. 5(c) : la region est a tracer par le candidat : le corrige decrit le trace (droites, sommets, cote a ombrer).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Given that each Mathematics text book costs 2400 FCFA and each English text book costs 3200 FCFA, show that $3x+4y\le24$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The total cost of the books cannot exceed the money available:

$2400x+3200y\le19\,200.$

Divide every term by $800$:

$3x+4y\le24.$ $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Given also that the number of English text books must be at most 75% of the number of Mathematics text books, write down another inequality in terms of $x$ and $y$ that satisfies this condition. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
75% of the number of Mathematics books is $0.75x=\dfrac34x$. The number of English books is at most this:

$y\le\dfrac34x$, that is **$4y\le3x$** (or $3x-4y\ge0$).

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) On a graph paper, taking 2 cm to represent 1 unit on both axes, shade so as to leave unshaded the region satisfied by these inequalities. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The numbers of books cannot be negative, so we also have $x\ge0$ and $y\ge0$. Use $0\le x\le8$ (16 cm) and $0\le y\le6$ (12 cm) with 2 cm per unit.

Boundary lines:

- $3x+4y=24$: passes through $(8,0)$ and $(0,6)$. Test $(0,0)$: $0\le24$ is true, so the required side contains the origin; shade the side away from the origin.
- $4y=3x$ (that is $y=\tfrac34x$): passes through $(0,0)$ and $(4,3)$. Test $(4,0)$: $0\le12$ is true, so the required side is the side **below** the line (towards the $x$-axis); shade the side above the line.
- $x$-axis ($y=0$) and $y$-axis ($x=0$): shade the sides $y<0$ and $x<0$.

The two lines meet where $3x+4y=24$ and $y=\tfrac34x$: $3x+3x=24\Rightarrow x=4,\ y=3$.

**The unshaded region is the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(8,0)$ and $(4,3)$** (plotted at $(0,0)$, $(16,0)$ and $(8,6)$ in centimetres), boundaries included.

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Hence, find the maximum number of text books the ex-student can buy. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The number of books is $N=x+y$, which is largest at a vertex of the region (or at a whole-number point of it). Evaluate $N$ at the vertices:

| Vertex | $N=x+y$ |
|---|---|
| $(0,0)$ | $0$ |
| $(8,0)$ | $8$ |
| $(4,3)$ | $7$ |

The maximum is $N=8$ at $(8,0)$. This is a whole-number point, and it satisfies both inequalities: $3(8)+4(0)=24\le24$ and $0\le\tfrac34(8)=6$. It costs $8\times2400=19\,200$ FCFA, exactly the money available.

**The maximum number of text books is 8** (8 Mathematics books and no English book).

If the student insisted on buying at least one English book, the whole-number points $(6,1)$, $(5,2)$ and $(4,3)$ all give $N=7$.
